issues.quote: Félix laughed and said it was his father's watch and was entitled to its opinions.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that Félix's watch showed twenty minutes to nine. It does not say the watch belonged to anyone else.
issues.misreading: The transcript makes Félix's watch his late father's watch, and the next lines say that watch has 'run badly for ten years.' A solver could reasonably conclude that the 8:40 reading is unreliable and discount it, when the sheet gives it as a plain reading at the nine o'clock bell.

issues.quote: I do not look at clocks when I am playing.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that she did not look at the clock when the doctor went out. It says nothing about her habits while playing in general.
issues.misreading: The sentence extends the no-clock-check claim to the whole time she played. A solver could take it to mean she had no way of knowing the time during the piano playing, which the sheet does not say.
